newsitem.title: UK: Gen Eaux eyes UK rail, sees profits up.
newsitem.headline: Gen Eaux eyes UK rail, sees profits up.

text.p: Generale des Eaux, the French utilities, construction and communications group, plans to acquire up to 25 percent of the UK rail market, president Jean-Marie Messier said in a Financial Times interview.
Messier said the company was bidding for "virtually all" of the UK's regional rail franchises, but would "under no circumstances" seek more than a quarter of the market.

Messier predicted that 1997 net profits would be at least four billion French francs, well above 1994's record 3.44 billion francs. After last year's heavy losses, Messier is predicting 1996 operating profits of 3.7 billion and net profits of 1.8 billion.

The company also aims to lift its return on equity to 15 percent by 1999, and is bringing its accounting standards into line with international practice in a move that could be prelude to an eventual foreign listing, the newspaper said. Messier expected this to take two to three years.
The company aims to cut its more than 50 billion French franc debt by at least 10 to 15 billion francs, Messier reiterated.

To achieve this, most of its minority holdings are for sale, and Messier has also decided to quit catering and healthcare. One business for sale is Generale de Satne, Europe's biggest private hospital operator, the newspaper said.
The next year would also be decisive on the company's French cable interests, Messier said.
He added that the group's 20 percent stake in Canal Plus, the French pay-TV company, was strategic.
